newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after bonds rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after bonds rise.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Wednesday and traders said falling bond yields supported the positive trend of the stock market.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.64 percent, or 1.97 points, to 311.76 on an all-share turnover of 233 million shekels against 221 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.31 percent higher at 317.66.

"The market has been mixed since the beginning of the week. The fact that it is trying to consolidate but without success and the fact that when it declines it happens with falling volume shows that the positive trend is expected to continue," said Arik Rotstein at Bloch Rotstein Securities and Investments.

"The prosperity of the bond market supports the positve trend in the market. Yields on some CPI-linked long bonds have fallen to 3.8 percent which is simply amazing," said Amir Ayal Senior Investment Manger at Epsilon Securities.
"The mood is very optimistic and the only fear is that the sharp rise in Wall Street might lead to a strong correction that will spill over to the Israeli market," Rotstein said.

"One of the main factors affecting the market are the positive returns posted by the mutual funds. With falling bond yields and lower interest rates more money is expected to come into the market," he said.

Amir added that the recovery of the primary market might have a negative impact on trading. "It's crazy. The success of all the new offerings shows that institutional investors are willing to buy at any price even when there is no economic justification. This might eventually have a negative impact on the market," he said.
Elbit lost 0.50 percent to 1,227 agorot (Israeli cents). Elbit said on Wednesday that second quarter loss per share fell to $0.09 from $0.19 in the same period last year.
Elbit Medical Imaging fell 1.5 percent to 2,839 agorot. The company said on Wednesday that second quarter earnings per share rose to $0.12 from $0.10 a share a year earlier.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which rose 3.5 percent to 609 agorot on turnover of 12.9 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 818 agorot on turnover of 12.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to 38,924 agorto on volume of 10.3 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
